name: mcp-server-brime

tools.name: brime_search
tools.description: Search the web with Brime API. Returns ranked results from across the web plus an LLM-synthesized answer (when include_answer is enabled). Use for current facts, recent events, specific entity lookups, or any query where the model needs grounding from live web data. Pick depth=instant for quick lookups, depth=basic for typical use, depth=advanced for thorough multi-source synthesis.

tools.name: brime_extract
tools.description: Fetch one or more URLs and return clean LLM-optimized markdown. Handles JavaScript-rendered pages and PDFs, not just static HTML. Use after brime_search to pull the contents of a specific page the model decided it needs to read in depth, or when the user hands the agent a URL directly. Each URL returns up to ~30KB of markdown; longer pages are truncated. Failed URLs appear in the failed list with an error code (do not silently drop them).

urls.description: URLs to extract content from. 1-10 URLs per call.

tools.name: brime_research
tools.description:
Multi-round agent-based research with citations. Two depth modes:
  - basic (sync, ~5-30s): single tool-call round → SERP → BM25 → LLM answer with sources. Best for questions answerable in 1-3 search hops.
  - deep (async, 1-10 minutes): 1-8 rounds with deep-search prompting (RESOLUTION-FIRST for time-relative refs). Returns a job_id IMMEDIATELY; you must poll with brime_research_status to get the result. Best for comparison questions, multi-entity synthesis, or anything needing several search hops.

When using deep mode, after this tool returns a job_id, call brime_research_status repeatedly (wait 30 seconds between calls) until status is 'complete', 'errored', or 'timeout'.

tools.name: brime_research_status
tools.description: Check the status of an async deep research job started by brime_research(depth='deep'). Returns one of: 'queued' / 'running' (still in progress — wait 30+ seconds and try again), 'complete' (final answer + sources included), 'errored' or 'timeout' (terminal failure). Stop polling once a terminal status is reached.

job_id.description: The job_id from a deep research start.

tools.name: brime_set_key
tools.description: Save the user's Brime API key on this machine so all future Brime tool calls work without configuration. Use this tool ONLY after another Brime tool (search, extract, research) has returned a 'no_api_key' error OR the user has explicitly given you a new key. Always ask the user for the key first — never make one up. Keys start with "sk-brime-". Free keys at https://platform.brime.dev/keys.

key.description: The Brime API key. Must start with "sk-brime-".
